author: Claude
note: Rubric and reference model for every child-facing game. Criteria come from the design-language rules; the rating rule is deterministic; patterns are hash-bound and go stale when their code changes. Scores and patterns are evidence for development choices, never acceptance.

criteria.title: Reachable in normal play
criteria.meets: A child reaches it from a fresh save by touch through a picture route (room, door, card or character), with no debug menu, playtest launcher or reading, and leaving returns to where it began.
criteria.partial: Reachable, but only after an undiscoverable or adult-only step, or with an unproven return.

criteria.title: True 2D
criteria.meets: Its own runtime path is Canvas only (Node2D, Control, Sprite2D, TextureRect, Camera2D); no 3D node, mesh, light, spatial shader or 3D vector state.
criteria.partial: Canvas gameplay that still depends on a 3D host, a 3D helper or a few spatial calls.
criteria.fails: The activity itself is built from 3D nodes, meshes or spatial movement.

criteria.title: Non-reader objectives
criteria.meets: Every required step has an exact spoken cue and a live pointer or diegetic cue at the actionable object; nothing needs reading.
criteria.partial: Most steps are spoken and pointed; one or more use a generic cheer, a wrong noun, a missing recording or a stale pointer.
criteria.fails: Objectives depend on text, or several steps have no exact voice or pointer.

criteria.title: One-finger generous input
criteria.meets: One finger taps, holds or drags only where the fiction asks; targets are at least 110x110 base pixels or an equivalent hit region; one touch owns one route.
criteria.partial: One-finger, but with a small target, a precise drag or a competing control.
criteria.fails: Needs steering, the virtual stick, simultaneous controls or precision a four-year-old lacks.

criteria.title: Kind no-fail and real agency
criteria.meets: No loss, timeout or lost item; mistakes get kind feedback; zero input never wins; correct play beats mashing; help widens or demonstrates without making mashing best.
criteria.partial: No loss, but a passive or mashing path is unguarded, or threat is not softened enough.
criteria.fails: A fail state, a punitive timer, or a win without the child acting.

criteria.title: Truthful action
criteria.meets: Each touch belongs to the visible object, the object really changes (pours from its spout, opens, fills), and when Roshan works she goes to the place and acts there before progress counts.
criteria.partial: Real state changes, but some steps act remotely, bounce generically, or disagree with the art.
criteria.fails: Progress comes from a detached cursor, a generic sparkle, or motion that contradicts the art (for example pouring backwards).

criteria.title: Authored art and identity
criteria.meets: Approved painted art staged as owned cards, one focal action, Roshan from the approved atlas family, always visible and in her own colours; and every overdraw check OD1-OD6 passes on measured states.
criteria.partial: Mostly authored and identity intact, but an overdraw check fails or has not been measured, or a known atlas defect remains.
criteria.fails: Placeholder shapes stand in for objects, duplicates sit over painted copies, or the owner has rejected the look.

criteria.title: Feedback and earned reward
criteria.meets: A valid touch shows a response at once; sight and sound describe the same event; effects never hide the action; stars and medals come only from intentional or explicitly assisted correct play.
criteria.partial: Feedback exists but is late, mismatched, hidden by effects, or rewards are loosely tied to play.
criteria.fails: Touches go unanswered, or rewards arrive without the child's action.

criteria.title: Lifecycle and save safety
criteria.meets: Start, finish, leave, re-enter, pause and focus loss are clean; held input is cancelled; timers, tweens and audio are owned and freed; save keys are only added; replay is idempotent; the room's music is restored.
criteria.partial: Works on the main path with a known leak, an unproven pause or re-entry, or shared state on the coordinator.
criteria.fails: Progress can be lost, input sticks after leaving, or re-entry breaks.

criteria.title: Machine verification
criteria.meets: A trusted probe drives real input through every step, includes a zero-input negative leg and checks teardown. Review captures and device sessions are acceptance evidence under C12, not part of this score.
criteria.partial: A trusted probe covers the main path but writes state directly, lacks the passive leg, or skips teardown.

criteria.title: No open defect
criteria.meets: No game-specific finding is open as a defect.
criteria.partial: Only P2/P3 defects, unconfirmed reports, owner decisions or external blocks remain.
criteria.fails: A game-specific P0 or P1 defect is open.

criteria.title: Device, child and owner acceptance
criteria.meets: The target phone session, an observed child session and the owner's acceptance are all recorded for this game.
criteria.partial: One or two of the three are recorded.
criteria.fails: None is recorded, or one of them did not accept.

rating_rule: 5 needs every criterion at 2, including recorded device, child and owner acceptance, and every overdraw check passed. 1 when a child cannot reach the game (C1 = 0). 2 when two or more of C2-C10 fail, or a game-specific P0 blocker is open. 3 when one of C2-C10 fails, a game-specific P0/P1 defect is open (C11 = 0), more than two of C1-C10 are only partly met, a core criterion (C1, C3, C4, C5, C6) is below 2, or an overdraw check fails or is unmeasured. Otherwise 4: core criteria met, overdraw checks passed, at most two partial criteria, and only device, child and owner gates left. C7 is capped at 1 until every overdraw check passes.

reference.why: The strongest true-2D game a child can reach today (Grand Puff scores more points but its fight is built on 3D nodes, so it cannot be a template) and the clearest model of the owner's 2026-09-06 job rule: Roshan travels to each part, her hand makes contact, and only then does the authored dirt clear; every part has its own line; every change saves; real-touch probes guard it. It contains the strongest single activity in the game (the waterfall), and its gaps are specific and fixable, so it is the first candidate for a full gold star and the template for room jobs and job games.
reference.status: CANDIDATE_REFERENCE: the Pool's own code meets every machine-assessed criterion and supplies most reference patterns. On 2026-10-04 Claude repaired the overdraw that shared room layers drew on its screen (MA-VIS-009, carved from MA-VIS-008, fixed pending verification): every play state now measures 1.18-1.41 mean layers with no duplicate, code drawing or translucent wash, and the reported 255-layer burst was a meter artifact, now corrected. It is 3/5 (21/24) until the OD2 look-alike review is recorded from Codex's phone-size captures (P1 in docs/handoffs/codex_pool_five_star_2026-10-04/README.md); then only device, child and owner acceptance remain.

patterns.title: Travel, contact, then credit
patterns.copy: Request travel to the real work point, follow Roshan's hand, and award progress only after the hand has been in contact for the work time; cancel on stop and focus loss.

patterns.title: A hand-anchored tool measured on the art
patterns.copy: Attach the tool to Roshan's measured hand socket and register its working point from pixel coordinates in the tool art, so contact means the tool, not the finger.

patterns.title: Save every change; a restored finish completes once
patterns.copy: Persist the part mask on every change and rebuild from it on entry; a fully restored mask emits completion exactly once.

patterns.title: One exact line per part and an approved hand at the live part
patterns.copy: Speak the current part's own instruction when it becomes active, and let the approved guide hand demonstrate the real verb on that part, not at a screen corner.

patterns.title: The fixture is the hit region; one touch owns the gesture
patterns.copy: Make the whole visible fixture (plus a margin) the touch target and keep the first touch as the owner until release or cancel.

patterns.title: A deliberate stroke beats repeated taps
patterns.copy: Let a purposeful drag finish a part in one motion while taps make small capped progress, so careful play is fastest and mashing never is.

patterns.title: Authored dirt over the real clean fixture
patterns.copy: Lay the authored dirty state over the untouched clean fixture and wipe it away where the child works, so progress is shown by the art itself and the finished room is the approved art.

patterns.title: Real-touch probe with far-touch, second-finger and cancel legs
patterns.copy: Drive the activity with pushed touch events, prove a far touch earns nothing, a second finger cannot steal the gesture, cancel clears it and re-entry restores it.

patterns.title: Taps that arrive mid-work wait their turn
patterns.copy: When the child taps while Roshan is already working, queue a bounded number of further actions and answer each tap at once; every queued action still needs its own contact time, and cancellation drops the unearned queue.

patterns.title: A quiet child hears the exact line again, twice at most
patterns.copy: After a quiet stretch, replay the activity's own exact lines (the other line first, then the hint) under a fresh voice session, at most twice per activity, while the guide hand keeps pointing; quiet time never earns progress.

patterns.title: Keep the character's colours under a room tint
patterns.copy: When a room is tinted to look dirty, give each of the character's cutouts inside the tinted tree the exact inverse, and fade both together, so the place changes but her identity colours do not.

patterns.title: A spoken line must be true of what just happened
patterns.copy: Choose each feedback line from what the child actually did (the object picked, the count reached), prefer an exact per-object take when it exists, and stay silent rather than name the wrong thing.

patterns.title: A room that authors its dirt opts out of shared code-drawn dirt
patterns.copy: When a room's activity shows the dirty state through authored art and a declared room tint (with the character counter-tinted, GS-17), list the room so the shared code-drawn wash, grime and cracks are hidden there; keep the shared layer's approved cutouts.

patterns.title: A focused activity quiets shared ambient layers while it is mounted
patterns.copy: Join the living-world quiet group while the activity owns the room's motion and guidance, so shared code-drawn ambience pauses above it and returns by itself when the activity is freed.

patterns.title: The reward beat plays out before the next scene takes the screen
patterns.copy: Hold the completion that starts a story clip or handoff until the reward's authored acting and spoken line have played, with a minimum and a hard maximum, polled in the owner's process so teardown can never resume a freed coroutine.

patterns.title: An affordance marks only what can be touched now
patterns.copy: Choose pulse or halo targets from hotspots that are visible in the tree, so an activity that suspends a hotspot layer is never undercut by an invitation the room cannot answer.

patterns.title: End-to-end real-touch driver through the world
patterns.copy: Complete the whole job from the room object to the reward with real touch events, including a multi-touch leg, inside a trusted probe.

patterns.title: Per-finger ownership with a focus-loss cancel
patterns.copy: Track each touch index, ignore a second finger while one owns the action, and cancel held input on focus loss and close.

patterns.title: Required lines refuse a generic fallback
patterns.copy: List each required objective key and refuse the generic cheer when its recording is missing, so a missing line shows up as a gap instead of a yay.

patterns.title: A per-phase checkpoint that awards once
patterns.copy: Checkpoint each finished phase as validated JSON, restore it only when the board reopens, and clear it after the win so a reward is never paid twice.

patterns.title: Medals from honest play statistics
patterns.copy: Compute bronze, silver and gold from misses, help and time measured during play, never from a timer or repeated taps.

patterns.title: A live-input gate with mercy that never wins alone
patterns.copy: Count a success only if the child touched within the last moment, and widen windows after misses without ever completing by itself.

overdraw.status: CANDIDATE_CRITERIA: refined 2026-10-04 at the owner's request; budgets are starting values the owner may change.
overdraw.measured_by: python -B tools/measure_overdraw.py (scripts/probe_overdraw.gd in a Mobile-renderer window; numbers only). Since 2026-10-04 an item spawned during the counted frames counts once like every other layer (it had drawn in its real colours and read as up to 255 layers), and a script-less layer that draws through a connected draw callback counts as code drawing; both are proven by the self-test.
overdraw.meaning: Overdraw is anything drawn over approved art that duplicates, competes with or muddies it, and the GPU cost of layers drawn under other layers. The owner rejected Chef for it (2026-10-03: "Chef still looks bad, lots of overdraw").

checks.title: One copy of everything
checks.means: Every object and state is drawn once: no texture drawn twice over itself, no live object over a painted copy of itself, no old state left under a new one. The only allowed stack is a reveal (authored dirt over the clean fixture it uncovers).
checks.method: Machine: no duplicate texture pair (same source region, at least 30% overlap) in any measured state. Review: no live object over a painted copy in the backdrop (MA-VIS-007).

checks.title: No look-alikes beside the action
checks.means: Painted objects that resemble the active object (the rack cakes behind Chef) are not near Roshan or the object being worked.
checks.method: Review at phone size with the HUD showing.

checks.title: No code-drawn shapes on screen
checks.means: Nothing on screen is drawn as code shapes over the art, except the child's own marks (paint strokes, traced trails) listed as allowed with a reason.
checks.method: Machine: every code-drawing script visible in a measured state must be classified allowed in this section's code_drawing list.

checks.title: Effects small and short
checks.means: Highlights, sparkles, bubbles and rings sit at the contact point, cover at most a quarter of Roshan, clear within a second and never stay over finished work.
checks.method: Machine: items that appear after an action are sampled for 2 s; transient ones must clear within effect_seconds and cover at most effect_over_roshan of her; no translucent item may linger. Guide hands are judged under C3.

checks.title: No broad translucent layers
checks.means: No full-screen spotlight, dimming, wash, vignette or glow. A room may look dingy only through a declared tint, with Roshan kept in her own colours.
checks.method: Machine: in every play state at least half the screen has no translucent layer (GPU translucent median 0), and no translucent layer covers half the screen.

checks.title: Fill budget and no wasted layers
checks.means: Few layers per pixel, and nothing drawn while hidden under opaque art.
checks.method: Machine: in every play state the GPU median frame has mean at most mean_layers, at least four layers on at most share_ge4 of the screen and max at most max_layers; no sampled frame exceeds peak_layers; no layer covering half the screen is drawn while 90% hidden.
